Does prior-installment growth (franchise momentum) predict crossing a $98–100M opening threshold better than contemporaneous competitor strength? US 2000-2025
Cases where a sequel showed strong momentum from prior installment but failed to reach ~$100M opening due to same-weekend tentpole competition, US 2000-2025
Correlation between marketing/network indicators (social media engagement, pre-sales/advance ticketing) and domestic opening weekend grosses for tentpoles, US 2015-2025

evenements.resolution: La question résoudra à OUI si, dans la fiche Box Office Mojo consultée pour Dune: Part Three au premier relevé non‑préliminaire, la valeur 'Opening weekend' domestique est strictement supérieure à $98,500,000 ; sinon ce sera NO.

source_resolution.document: table 'Top Opening Weekends' / page du film Dune: Part Three sur Box Office Mojo — la valeur 'Opening weekend (domestic)' publiée
source_resolution.regle_ambiguite: utiliser la valeur 'Opening weekend' domestique telle que Box Office Mojo la publie pour le film, en prenant la première valeur non‑préliminaire disponible; si Box Office Mojo n'indique pas de valeur définitive au moment de la résolution, appliquer la valeur la plus récente non‑préliminaire fournie par Box Office Mojo.

programme.extrait: Simultaneous releases of two tent‑pole films rarely knock a partner’s opening‑weekend gross down by more than 15 %.
When the audiences overlap, the weaker film tends to suffer the >15 % loss (as seen with *Hollow Man*, *Cloverfield*, *Big Hero 6*).
This supports the conclusion that **most tent‑poles are resilient** to competition.
